request.summary: S2 minimal formal wire promotion and static Adapter diagnostics are sound on code inspection; no new production correctness/leakage defect found in those branches. Two P2 findings prevent clean S2 acceptance: relative oracle paths still load an old EXE, and current evidence/coverage does not establish the required artifact provenance, complete Projection leakage checks or same-business-fixture usage/visible-content invariance. Prior full-suite and format limits remain; no disposition or progression performed.

source_revision.scope: Current uncommitted S2 formal vendor/decode/Adapter/helper/tests/fixtures/docs. 13 captured execution attachments all match current bytes; additional 10 inputs/docs are hashed at this review. Unrelated workflow-system edits and S1 staging changes are not newly reviewed or reverted.

findings.title: Enforce absolute oracle paths and preserve the selected artifact provenance
findings.body: explicit_oracle_binary only checks is_file(). It accepts a relative path, although the adopted S2 work requires explicit absolute paths. The supplemental probe selected native/codex-rollout-demo/target/debug/codex-rollout-demo.exe (old 2026-08-25 artifact, SHA256 77c78d22c08a116b99320249c9a504c83fb82d058e3f8ec303f21512eb5baaf6) through a relative TERMLINK_STAGE3_DEMO_BIN and the actual oracle selector passed. The S2 execution and linked test/CR state only 'explicit binaries' and 5/5; they do not retain the actual two variable values, selected paths/hashes, build-input/profile/target-dir association, or a link identifying the reused S1 artifacts. The execution's 13 source snapshots establish source identity, but cannot establish the artifacts selected by that past run. Do not certify that historical 5/5 run as fresh merely from source snapshot parity or this review's current artifact hashes.
findings.consequence: A passing actual-oracle comparison can still use an old reference binary and fail to prove the adopted current-subject acceptance requirement.
findings.recommendation: Reject non-absolute explicit paths without fallback. In the actual acceptance caller record/check both absolute task-private paths, existence/hash and successful build provenance, linking the S1 build record if reusing its exact outputs; retain a no-fallback counterexample. Recover existing actual evidence if available rather than inventing values or rerunning business work just for a receipt.
findings.supplemental_checks: Both nonexistent explicit Demo and Spike paths returned exit 1 at the explicit-path assertion while old default EXEs exist. Relative old Demo path returned exit 0 / 1 passed. These are direct executions of the existing S2 test EXE, not a fresh Cargo build or certification of the historical positive run.

findings.title: Check full Projection leakage and usage invariance against the carrier-free control
findings.body: The developer test scans only serialized AnalysisBatch. Neither new test constructs/scans the full AnalysisProjection required by adopted S2. The usage test merely asserts that some legacy UsageUpdated (120/70) and RateLimitUpdated (12.5%) exist; an additional UsageUpdated from token_usage_record would still satisfy it. The two-record usage fixture has no user/assistant/tool content or turn lifecycle, and there is no comparison to the same business fixture without the new carrier. It therefore does not exercise the required visible-content/per-turn/session usage invariance or prove absence of a second accounting source.
findings.consequence: Current 33/33 conformance count does not cover the promised Projection hidden-content boundary or duplicate usage regression. This is a coverage finding, not an assertion that current static-diagnostic Adapter branches actually leak or double count.
findings.recommendation: Extend the existing focused conformance tests to reduce/serialize the full Projection and check developer body/internal metadata and cumulative payload sentinels. Compare retained visible content and per-turn/session usage/rate values, plus UsageUpdated count, for the same business fixture with and without token_usage_record. Make the checks demonstrably reject injected leak/extra usage outcomes in temporary data or focused tests; preserve true unknown/malformed fail-closed coverage.
